root.name: Zukertort Opening: Reversed Grünfeld
root.moves: 1. Nf3 d5 2. g3 c5 3. Bg2 Nc6 4. d4

overview: White fianchettoes against ...d5 and ...c5, then strikes with 4.d4 to challenge Black's centre. Black can take on d4 (4...cxd4 5.Nxd4) or defend with ...Nf6 and ...e6, reaching a Catalan-like or Grünfeld-reversed structure with White castling and playing c4 later. The game is positional, with tension on the d- and c-pawns.

white_ideas.idea: Castle, then play c4 or dxc5 to open the long diagonal and press on the queenside.
Use the fianchettoed bishop and Nbd2/Nc3 to pressure d5 and the c-file.

black_ideas.idea: Hold the centre with ...Nf6, ...e6 and ...Be7 and answer with ...cxd4 or ...c4.
Gain space with ...c4 and hold the bishop pair.

typical_structures.structure: Black pawns on c5 and d5 against White d4; hanging pawns or an isolated pawn appear after exchanges.

character.notes: Strategic play around central tension; not a mutual attack.

structure.notes: Centre pawns in tension; the structure can become an IQP, hanging pawns or a closed centre.

approach.notes: A less common move order but used by strong players, like the Réti.

sublines_that_differ.name: 4...cxd4
sublines_that_differ.how: Black challenges the knight and the position becomes more open.

character.reason: Strategic with central tension but no forcing theory.

approach.reason: Used by strong players as a Réti-type option.
